questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are papers. Some cartons are utensils. Conclusion (I): No box is a utensil. Conclusion (II): Some papers are utensils.
questions.explanation: Some cartons are utensils and all cartons are papers, so some papers are utensils (II). Some boxes are cartons, but nothing rules out a box being a utensil, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BELL' is written as 'MKFA' and 'BOND' is written as 'EMPA'. How will 'BLEW’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse, then its letters move +1, −1, +1, −1: BELL → LLEB → MKFA and BOND → DNOB → EMPA. So BLEW → WELB → XDMA.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In AFK, LQV and DIN each letter is 5 places after the one before it. In PTX the steps are 4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: 10 is related to 15 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 42 is related to 63. To which of the following numbers is 22 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to 1.5 times itself: 10 → 15 and 42 → 63. So 22 → 33.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘sit on chair’ is coded as 'sk mi cn' and ‘the chair broke’ is coded as ‘gm fr mi’. How is ‘chair’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'chair' is the only word in both sentences and 'mi' the only code in both, so chair = mi.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (79, 58, 62) (54, 33, 37) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is the first minus 21 and the third is the second plus 4: 79 → 58 → 62 and 54 → 33 → 37. Likewise 66 → 45 → 49.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the option that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed).
questions.explanation: In 2 – 2 – 4, 1 – 3 – 3 and 2 – 4 – 8 the third number is the product of the first two. In 3 – 2 – 5 it is their sum (3 × 2 = 6), so it does not belong.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. FM61, EK58, DI55, CG52, ?
questions.explanation: First letters run F, E, D, C, so next is B; second letters move back two (M, K, I, G), so next is E; the number falls by 3 (61, 58, 55, 52), so next is 49: BE49.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (7, 9, 48) (6, 8, 42) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is three times the sum of the first two: (7 + 9) × 3 = 48 and (6 + 8) × 3 = 42. Likewise (11 + 13) × 3 = 72.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 18 − 23 × 455 ÷ 7 + 28 = 377

Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. L M B A _ H O L M B A C _ O L M _ A C H O L _ B A C H O L _
questions.explanation: With C, H, B, M, M in the blanks the block LMBACHO repeats: LMBACHO LMBACHO LMBACHO LMBACHO LM.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘PRANKED’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: PRANKED in alphabetical order is A D E K N P R. Position by position no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A # B means A is the sister of B. A @ B means A is the son of B. A & B means A is the wife of B. A % B means A is the father of B. How is Q related to R if P & Q % L # R & K?
questions.explanation: P is the wife of Q, Q is the father of L, L is the sister of R and R is the wife of K. L and R are both Q's children, so Q is R's father.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘–’ are interchanged? 4 − 12 + 3 ÷ 12 × 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 × 12 ÷ 3 + 12 − 6 = 16 + 12 − 6 = 22.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZVRN, VSPM, RPNL, ?, JJJJ
questions.explanation: Letter by letter the clusters move back by fixed steps: first letters −4 (Z, V, R, N, J), second −3 (V, S, P, M, J), third −2 (R, P, N, L, J) and fourth −1 (N, M, L, K, J). The missing cluster is NMLK.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 23, 27, 43, 79, 143, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 16, 36 and 64, the squares of 2, 4, 6 and 8. Next is 10² = 100: 143 + 100 = 243.

questions.text: Which government honoured a distinguished percussionist named Pandit Anindo Chatterjee with the Banga Vibhushan Award in 2022?
questions.explanation: In 2022 the West Bengal government gave its Banga Vibhushan award to tabla player Pandit Anindo Chatterjee.

questions.text: According to the Indian Railways (2019-2020), which state has the largest railway track in India?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh has the longest railway network of any state.

questions.text: Who was appointed as India’s 28th Controller General of Accounts (CGA) in March 2023?
questions.explanation: S. S. Dubey took charge as the 28th Controller General of Accounts in March 2023.

questions.text: After the death of Humayun, the 13 year-old Akbar was coronated in 1556 at Kalanaur in ________.
questions.explanation: Akbar was crowned in 1556 at Kalanaur, in the Gurdaspur district of Punjab.

questions.text: Which Five-Year Plan primarily focused on the 'Garibi Hatao' initiative?
questions.explanation: The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-79) put the removal of poverty ('Garibi Hatao') and self-reliance at its centre.

questions.text: In which of the following cities of Manipur is the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy located?
questions.explanation: The Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy, a unit of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, is in Imphal.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Governor-General of British India helped Raja Ram Mohan Roy legally abolish the sati practice?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck's Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 made sati illegal, after Raja Ram Mohan Roy's campaign against it.

questions.text: Mahabalipuram emerged as an important centre of temple architecture under which of the following kingdoms of south India?
questions.explanation: The Pallava kings, notably Narasimhavarman I and Rajasimha, built Mahabalipuram's rock-cut rathas and the Shore Temple.

questions.text: Which of the following was the mascot of the FIH men’s Hockey World Cup – 2023?
questions.explanation: The mascot of the 2023 FIH Men's Hockey World Cup, held in Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha, was 'Olly'.

questions.text: By which of the following state governments is the Tansen Music Festival organised?
questions.explanation: The Tansen Samaroh, held every year at Gwalior near Tansen's tomb, is organised by the Madhya Pradesh government.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: They are positive, as they require the State to do certain things.
These have moral and political sanctions.
They aim at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
They promote welfare of individuals. Hence, they are personal and individualistic.
questions.explanation: Directive Principles aim at the welfare of the community as a whole; it is the Fundamental Rights that are individualistic. So the last statement is incorrect.

questions.text: The Indian Constitution has established _________.
questions.explanation: The Constitution sets up a single, integrated judiciary that is independent of the executive and the legislature; unlike the USA, India has no separate federal and state court systems.

questions.text: Which of the following is a non-perishable food?
questions.explanation: Dry pulses keep for months without spoiling; curd, meat and milk spoil within days.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT correct with regards to the history of calculating National Income (NI) in India?
options: Dadabhai Naoroji divided the Indian economy into two parts: primary sector and secondary sector.
First attempt to compute NI was made by Dadabhai Naoroji.
First official attempt to compute NI was made by PC Mahalanobis.
First scientific method to compute NI was used by Dr VKRV Rao.
questions.explanation: The other three are the standard facts: Naoroji made the first estimate of national income (1867-68), V. K. R. V. Rao first used a scientific method, and the National Income Committee under P. C. Mahalanobis made the first official estimate. SSC's key marks the statement about Naoroji's two-sector division as the incorrect one.

questions.text: Hubbardia heptaneuron, which has become endangered, is a species of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Hubbardia heptaneuron is an endangered grass of the Western Ghats, known from the spray zone of the Jog Falls in Karnataka.

questions.text: The Parliament passed the Marine Aids to Navigation Bill, 2021 to repeal and replace which of the following Acts?
questions.explanation: The Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021 replaced the nearly century-old Lighthouse Act, 1927.

questions.text: When was the 1st Asian Kabaddi Championship held?
questions.explanation: The first Asian Kabaddi Championship was held in 1980 in Kolkata (then Calcutta).

questions.text: The climate of a place is NOT affected by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Climate depends on location (latitude), relief and altitude, and distance from the sea; the type of soil does not affect it.

questions.text: In which musical note did Newland put the metals Co and Ni with halogens?
questions.explanation: In Newlands' table of octaves, cobalt and nickel share a place in the 'Do' column with the halogens fluorine, chlorine and bromine, one of the table's anomalies.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following places is related to Gandhi’s Satyagraha of the year 1917?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was at Champaran, Bihar, in 1917, for the indigo farmers. Kheda and the Ahmedabad mill strike came in 1918, Bardoli in 1928.

questions.text: Which of the following is in geographical proximity to Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: Karaikal, a part of Puducherry on the Tamil Nadu coast, is the closest to Sri Lanka; Yanam is in Andhra Pradesh and Mahe in Kerala.

questions.text: The decomposition of gaseous Ammonia on a hot platinum surface is a _______________ order reaction at high pressure.
questions.explanation: At high pressure the platinum surface is saturated with ammonia, so the rate does not depend on its concentration: a zero-order reaction.

questions.text: Which organisms are classified as Aves?
questions.explanation: Aves is the class of birds.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev?
questions.explanation: Gurpurab (Guru Nanak Jayanti), on Kartik Purnima, marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev.

questions.text: How many awards were presented at the National Sports and Adventure Awards-2022 ceremony held at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 30 November 2022?
questions.explanation: 44 awards were presented, including the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna to table tennis player Sharath Kamal and 25 Arjuna Awards.

questions.text: Kiran lent ₹4,000 to two persons such that one part of it at the rate of 8% per annum and the remaining part at the rate of 10% per annum. He got an annual simple interest of ₹352. Then the sum lent at 10% is:
By applying which of the following criteria can two triangles NOT be proved congruent?
questions.explanation: Two triangles with equal angles (AAA) are similar but can differ in size, so AAA does not prove congruence.

questions.text: X, Y, and Z are three points on a plane with XY = 11 cm, YZ = 13 cm, and XZ = 24 cm. The number of circles that travel through points X, Y, and Z is:
questions.explanation: XY + YZ = 11 + 13 = 24 = XZ, so Y lies on the segment XZ: the three points are collinear, and no circle passes through three collinear points.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest 5-digit number divisible by 47?
questions.explanation: 99999 ÷ 47 leaves remainder 30 (47 × 2127 = 99969), so the largest 5-digit multiple of 47 is 99999 − 30 = 99969.

questions.text: If, on a marked price, the difference between selling prices with a discount of 65% and with two successive discounts of 30% and 40% is ₹105, then the marked price (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: One 65% discount leaves 35% of the marked price; 30% then 40% leaves 0.7 × 0.6 = 42%. The difference, 7% of the marked price, is ₹105, so the marked price is ₹1,500.

questions.text: Three pipes P, Q and R can fill a cistern in 40 minutes, 80 minutes and 120 minutes, respectively. Initially, all the pipes are opened. After how much time (in minutes) should the pipes Q and R be turned off so that the cistern will be completely filled in just half an hour?
questions.explanation: P alone fills 30/40 = 3/4 of the cistern in 30 minutes. Q and R must fill the other 1/4 at 1/80 + 1/120 = 1/48 a minute, which takes 12 minutes.

questions.text: The ages of two friends, Ram and Ravi, differ by 7 years. Ram’s mother Mayadevi is three times as old as Ram, and Ravi is four times as old as his brother Soham. The ages of Mayadevi and Soham differ by 65 years. Find the age of Mayadevi (in years).
questions.explanation: Let Soham be s: Ravi = 4s, Mayadevi = s + 65 and Ram = (s + 65)/3. Ram − Ravi = 7 gives (s + 65)/3 − 4s = 7, so s = 4 and Mayadevi is 69 (Ram 23, Ravi 16).

questions.text: A money bag contains one rupee, 5 rupee and 10 rupee coins in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7 respectively. If the total amount in the bag is ₹980, then find the number of coins of ₹10.
questions.explanation: One set of 3 + 5 + 7 coins is worth 3 × 1 + 5 × 5 + 7 × 10 = ₹98. ₹980 is 10 such sets, so there are 7 × 10 = 70 coins of ₹10.

questions.text: If the sum of three numbers is 18 and the sum of their squares is 36, then find the difference between the sum of their cubes and three times of their product.
questions.explanation: a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). Here ab + bc + ca = (18² − 36)/2 = 144, so the value is 18 × (36 − 144) = −1944.

questions.text: In a circular race of 750 m, X and Y start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 9 km/h and 13.5 km/h, respectively. If they are running in the same direction then, when will they meet again for the first time on the track?
questions.explanation: The faster runner gains 13.5 − 9 = 4.5 km/h = 1.25 m/s. Gaining one full lap of 750 m takes 750/1.25 = 600 seconds.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The Morbi bridge mishap has left Gujarat in a “deplorable” state.
questions.explanation: 'Deplorable' means shockingly bad. Of the options only 'despicable' is close; 'rejoicing' and 'jubilation' point the other way.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A government by the officials
questions.explanation: Bureaucracy is government by officials who are not elected.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. I'm _______________ about whether to accept the job offer or continue freelancing. Both options have their advantages.
questions.explanation: To be 'on the fence' is to be undecided between two choices.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After the concert was over, / they go to a restaurant, / had dinner together / and talked until midnight.
questions.explanation: The other verbs are in the past ('was over', 'had', 'talked'), so 'they went to a restaurant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He was “trembling” with fear.
questions.explanation: 'Trembling' means shaking: 'shivering'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I have been living in Hyderabad “since I am born” .
questions.explanation: Birth is a finished past event, so 'since I was born'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who sells and arranges cut flowers.
questions.explanation: A florist sells and arranges cut flowers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. She was “elated” about her promotion, but her colleague felt quite disheartened.
questions.explanation: 'Elated' means very happy; its opposite is 'discouraged'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place where fruit trees are grown
questions.explanation: An orchard is land where fruit trees are grown.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A small group of people who spend their time together and do not welcome other people into that group
questions.explanation: A clique is a small, close group that keeps others out.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Renewable energy / sources like solar and wind power / will replaced traditional fossil fuels / and help reduce carbon emissions.
options: sources like solar and wind power
questions.explanation: After 'will' the verb takes its base form: 'will replace'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. More children go to school than at any time in the past. But more children today are out of school than any time in the past. B. But it is not enough to blame the high birth rate for this state of affairs. C. Indeed, it can be reasonably argued that continued mass illiteracy is not the result but the cause of the high birth rate. D. There are more literate people in India today than ever before. But there are also more illiterates than ever before.
questions.explanation: D opens with literacy in India, A extends the same pattern to schooling, B says the high birth rate alone cannot be blamed, and C ('Indeed') takes that point further: DABC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On the ball
options: Aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them
Unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but slow to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but doing nothing
questions.explanation: To be 'on the ball' is to be alert to what is happening and quick to react.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Timid
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means shy and easily frightened; its opposite is 'daring'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The contract was grabbed by the biggest telecom company in India.
options: The biggest telecom company in India grabs the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India grabbed the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India will grab the contract.
The biggest telecom company in India has grabbed the contract.
questions.explanation: 'Was grabbed by' is simple past passive, so the active is 'The biggest telecom company in India grabbed the contract.'

questions.text: The following sentence contains a word with a spelling error. Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the identified word from the given options. He has to be conscious of his public manners as he is a decendent of a reputed family in this region.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'descendant'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. By whom was grammar taught to you?
options: You were taught grammar by whom?
questions.explanation: 'By whom was grammar taught to you?' is the passive of 'Who taught you grammar?'

questions.text: Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word. Equivocal
questions.explanation: 'Equivocal' means open to more than one interpretation: 'ambiguous'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Entrepreneurship' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'colleague', 'consensus' and 'bizarre'.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? ICT, FES, CGR, ZIQ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (I, F, C, Z, so next W); second letters forward 2 (C, E, G, I, so K); third letters back 1 (T, S, R, Q, so P): WKP.

questions.text: Select the pair in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as are the numbers in the given pairs. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 12 : 25 11 : 23
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 1: 12 × 2 + 1 = 25 and 11 × 2 + 1 = 23. Likewise 21 × 2 + 1 = 43.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. DOY:PAK ::BQM:NCY :: ILU:?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 12 places forward, wrapping round after Z: D → P, O → A, Y → K and B → N, Q → C, M → Y. So I → U, L → X and U → G: UXG.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TIZZ’ is written as ‘VKBB’ and ‘QOPH’ is written as ‘SQRJ’. How will ‘CKAU’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward (Z wraps round to B): TIZZ → VKBB and QOPH → SQRJ. So CKAU → EMCW.

questions.text: 104 is related to 13 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 136 is related to 17. To which of the following is 232 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its eighth: 104 ÷ 8 = 13 and 136 ÷ 8 = 17. So 232 ÷ 8 = 29.

questions.text: Each vowel in the word ‘SIMILAR’ is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the second from the left end and the third from the left end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.explanation: With consonants moved back one and vowels forward one, SIMILAR becomes R J L J K B Q. The second and third letters are J and L, with one letter, K, between them.

questions.text: Three of the following number-pairs are alike in some manner and hence form a group. Which number-pair does not belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 18 – 306, 22 – 462 and 21 – 420 the second number is the first times one less than itself (18 × 17, 22 × 21, 21 × 20). 15 – 240 is 15 × 16, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. D F _ I J O D _ H I J O _ F H I J O D F _ I J O D _
questions.explanation: With H, F, D, H, F in the blanks the block DFHIJO repeats: DFHIJO DFHIJO DFHIJO DFHIJO DF.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 116 - 92 ÷ 4 + 25 × 2 - 20 = 150

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (25, 300, 6) (19, 342, 9)
questions.explanation: In each set, first × third × 2 = second: 25 × 6 × 2 = 300 and 19 × 9 × 2 = 342. Likewise 18 × 8 × 2 = 288.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. BACK : CCBI : : TEST : UGRR : : WORK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, −1, −2: BACK → CCBI and TEST → UGRR. So WORK → XQQI.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 543, 518, 495, 474, 455, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −25, −23, −21, −19, shrinking by 2 each time, so the next is −17: 455 − 17 = 438.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COWS’ is coded as ‘7935’ and ‘OILY’ is coded as ‘2568’. What is the code for ‘O’ in that language?
questions.explanation: O is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so O = 5.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some bags are purses. All purses are wallets. All wallets are sacks. Conclusions: (I) All purses are sacks. (II) Some wallets are bags.
questions.explanation: All purses are wallets and all wallets are sacks, so all purses are sacks (I). The bags that are purses are wallets, so some wallets are bags (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 72 – 6 + (18 ÷ 4) + 17 – (22 × 2) = 44

In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A − B means ‘A is the father of B’. A × B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A ÷ B means ‘A is the wife of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P × Q + R ÷ S − T’?
questions.explanation: P is the mother of Q, Q is the brother of R, R is the wife of S and S is the father of T. So R is T's mother and P is R's mother: P is T's mother's mother.

questions.text: Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In BFJ, EIM and IMQ each letter is 4 places after the one before it. DHK moves +4 then +3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No bench is chair. All sofas are benches. All tables are sofas. Conclusions: I. No table is a chair. II. Some sofas are chairs. III. All tables are benches.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Tables are sofas and sofas are benches, so all tables are benches (III); and as no bench is a chair, no table is a chair (I). II cannot follow: every sofa is a bench, and no bench is a chair.

questions.text: Which of the following has the highest salinity?
questions.explanation: By NCERT's figures Lake Van in Turkey (330 parts per thousand) is saltier than the Dead Sea (238) and the Great Salt Lake (220); the Red Sea is far less salty than any of them.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following social reformers of 19th century India was the author of ‘Stree Purush Tulana’?
questions.explanation: Tarabai Shinde wrote 'Stree Purush Tulana' (1882), a sharp critique of how society treated women.

questions.text: Harela is a festival of greenery, peace, prosperity, and environmental conservation, primarily celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Harela is celebrated mainly in Uttarakhand, with saplings planted to mark the coming of the rains.

questions.text: Which state initiated the implementation of the Mid-day Meal scheme in elementary schools?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu pioneered the mid-day meal in its schools, long before the national scheme of 1995.

questions.text: In which of the following games is one player known as the Wicketkeeper?
questions.explanation: The wicketkeeper stands behind the stumps in cricket.

questions.text: ‘Au’ is the symbol for which of the following elements?
questions.explanation: Au, from the Latin 'aurum', is the symbol of gold; silver is Ag, aluminium Al and argon Ar.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is the author of the book, ‘The Indian Struggle’?
questions.explanation: 'The Indian Struggle' is Subhas Chandra Bose's account of the freedom movement from 1920.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants power to the President to appoint Judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2) every Judge of the Supreme Court is appointed by the President.

questions.text: Mohiniyattam is associated with which of the following traditional dance styles?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance, is performed in the graceful lasya style.

questions.text: As of March 2023, how many High Courts are there in India?
questions.explanation: India has 25 High Courts; the newest, for Andhra Pradesh, was set up in 2019.

questions.text: In which year was the International Olympic Committee formed?
questions.explanation: The International Olympic Committee was founded on 23 June 1894 in Paris, at the congress called by Pierre de Coubertin.

questions.text: Ustad Vilayat Ali Khan is a maestro in ________.
questions.explanation: Ustad Vilayat Khan was one of the great sitar players of the twentieth century.

questions.text: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas block the cold winds from Central Asia, keeping northern India warmer in winter.

questions.text: Which of the following is the transboundary river between India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Ravi, which runs along the India-Pakistan border for part of its course before entering Pakistan. (The Indus and the Jhelum also flow from India into Pakistan; the Beas lies wholly in India.)

questions.text: To which group do the alkaline earth metals such as radium, barium and strontium belong?
questions.explanation: Beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium are the alkaline earth metals of Group 2 (2A).

questions.text: According to the Agricultural and Processed food products Export Development Authority (APEDA) 2020-2021, which state of India has the first rank in grapes production?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra, above all the Nashik region, grows most of India's grapes.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions about the organisation of ‘Village Panchayats’?
questions.explanation: Article 40, a Directive Principle, asks the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution contains Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: Article 51A, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, lists the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: How many medals did India win in International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) World Cup 2022, which was held in Cairo, Egypt?
questions.explanation: India won 7 medals at the 2022 ISSF World Cup in Cairo.

questions.text: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?
questions.explanation: Pinctada margaritifera is the black-lip pearl oyster, the source of Tahitian black pearls.

questions.text: In the 7th Century AD, a new religion called Islam was born in _________.
questions.explanation: Islam began in Arabia in the 7th century AD, with the Prophet Muhammad's preaching at Mecca.

questions.text: Sitar maestro, Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded which of the following awards by the Government of India in 1999?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

questions.text: Gautamiputra Satakarni titled Rajaraja and Maharaja is related to which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the greatest of the Satavahana kings; his mother's Nashik inscription records his titles.

questions.text: Which of the following options is associated with the class of cold-blooded animals?
questions.explanation: A chameleon is a reptile, and reptiles are cold-blooded. Pavo (peafowl), Psittacula (parakeets) and Macropus (kangaroos) are birds and mammals, which are warm-blooded.

questions.text: The CSO adopted the concept of Gross Value Added in ______.
questions.explanation: In January 2015 the CSO released its new national accounts series (base year 2011-12), measuring sectors' output as gross value added.

questions.text: The concentrations of three acids, A, B, and C, are specified as 20%, 30%, and 40%, respectively. They are blended in a ratio of 3 : 5 : a, yielding a solution with a concentration of 30%. What is the value of 'a'?
Find the values of x, y and z, so as to satisfy the equations given below: x + y + z = 12; x + y – z = 6; x – y + z = 4
questions.explanation: Adding the first two equations: 2x + 2y = 18, so x + y = 9 and z = 3. Adding the first and third: 2x + 2z = 16, so x + z = 8, x = 5 and y = 4.

questions.text: A policeman noticed a thief at a distance of 500 metres. The policeman started running and the thief also started running at the same time. The thief is running at a speed of 15 km/h. It took 15 minutes for the policeman to catch the thief. Find the speed of the policeman (in km/h).
questions.explanation: The policeman closes 500 m = 0.5 km in 15 minutes (1/4 hour), so he gains 2 km/h on the thief: 15 + 2 = 17 km/h.

questions.text: ΔEFG and ΔHIJ are similar. Also, ∠E = ∠H and ∠F = ∠I. If 3EF = HI and FG = 9 cm, then IJ is equal to ____.
questions.explanation: Similar triangles have proportional sides. HI = 3EF, so each side of ΔHIJ is 3 times its match in ΔEFG and IJ = 3 × FG = 27 cm.

questions.text: If A:B = 6 : 8 and B:C = 5 : 12, then A:B:C is:
questions.explanation: A : B = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4 and B : C = 5 : 12. Making B the same (20): A : B = 15 : 20 and B : C = 20 : 48, so A : B : C = 15 : 20 : 48.

questions.text: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated about the sides of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
questions.explanation: Rotating about the 3 cm side gives a cone of height 3 cm and radius 4 cm: V = (1/3)π × 4² × 3 = 16π cm³.

questions.text: Two successive discounts of 40% and 30% are equal to a single discount of:
questions.explanation: After 40% and then 30% off, 0.6 × 0.7 = 0.42 of the price is left: a single discount of 58%.

questions.text: Ravi's salary was increased by 50%. After some time, his new salary was also increased by 50%. Find his gain percentage of salary.
questions.explanation: Two 50% rises multiply the salary by 1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25: a gain of 125%.

questions.text: If 45° and 65° are the angles of a triangle, then find the exterior angle of the third angle (remaining angle).
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: 45° + 65° = 110°.

questions.text: If (77⁷⁷ + 77) is divided by 78, then the remainder will be:
questions.explanation: 77 = 78 − 1, so 77⁷⁷ leaves remainder (−1)⁷⁷ = −1 on division by 78. Then 77⁷⁷ + 77 leaves −1 + 77 = 76.

questions.text: What annual instalment will discharge a debt of ₹26,160 due in 4 years at 6% simple interest p.a.?
questions.explanation: Each instalment x earns simple interest until the debt falls due: x(1.18) + x(1.12) + x(1.06) + x = 4.36x = ₹26,160, so x = ₹6,000.

questions.text: In a circle of radius 5√13 cm, a chord is at a distance of 10 cm from the centre of the circle. Find the length (in cm) of the chord.
questions.explanation: Half the chord = √(r² − d²) = √(325 − 100) = 15 cm, so the chord is 30 cm.

questions.text: Places A and B are 20 km apart on the highway. A car starts from A and another from B at the same time. If the cars travel in the same direction at different speeds, they meet in one hour. If they travelled towards each other, they met in 12 minutes. What are the speeds (in km/h) of two cars?
questions.explanation: Same direction: the difference of the speeds closes 20 km in 1 hour, so it is 20 km/h. Towards each other: their sum closes 20 km in 12 minutes (1/5 hour), so it is 100 km/h. The speeds are 60 and 40 km/h.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Their sporting achievements at the highest level are being “utterly” ignored.
questions.explanation: 'Utterly' means completely; its opposite is 'minimally'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Our family is planning / a trip to Europe next summer / where we should visit several famous / landmarks and enjoy local cuisine.
options: a trip to Europe next summer
where we should visit several famous
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a plan, so 'where we will visit'; 'should' expresses obligation or advice, which does not fit.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Risible
questions.explanation: 'Risible' means laughable; its opposite is 'serious'. 'Droll' (amusing) is close to a synonym.

questions.text: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: its first constitution P: and soon got himself elected Q: the administration of the country R: general Ayub Khan took over S: after Pakistan framed
questions.explanation: 'After Pakistan framed (S) its first constitution (O) general Ayub Khan took over (R) the administration of the country (Q) and soon got himself elected (P).'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The letter will be delivered by the postman tomorrow.
options: The postman delivered the letter tomorrow
The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow.
The postman will have delivered the letter tomorrow.
The postman will be delivering the letter tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Will be delivered by' is the future passive of 'will deliver': 'The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. He was an irresponsible person “to the matter of taking up” responsibilities.
options: in the matter of taking up
at the matter of taking up
by the matter of taking up
along the matter of taking up
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'in the matter of': 'irresponsible in the matter of taking up responsibilities'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pugnacious
questions.explanation: 'Pugnacious' means eager to fight: 'belligerent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Stationary
questions.explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving: 'still'. (Not to be confused with 'stationery', writing materials.)

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one word substitute for the given group of words. An often-imaginary place or state of utter perfection and happiness
questions.explanation: A utopia is an imagined place or state of perfection; a dystopia is its opposite.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is also called a nuclear family. B. It is good to be in a small family because there is better management of resources. C. A small family is one with parents and a maximum of two children. D. The advantages of a small family are numerous.
questions.explanation: C defines a small family, A gives its other name, D introduces its advantages and B gives one of them: CADB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. Most of the land near the town is “barren”, but the efforts of the farmers have turned it ________.
questions.explanation: 'Barren' land produces nothing; the farmers have made it 'fertile'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. Subir’s long absence is likely to have _____ for employees in the office.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'repercussions'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. delicious R. she Q. a P. baked S. chocolate cake
questions.explanation: 'She baked a delicious chocolate cake': RPQOS.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. Most of the flowers “bloom” in the spring season but they start to ________ during summer.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'bloom' is 'wither'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The shareholders will elect him a director.
options: The shareholders have elected him a director.
He will be elected as director by the shareholders.
The shareholders elected him a director.
He will be elected a director.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will elect' becomes 'will be elected', with the agent kept: 'He will be elected as director by the shareholders.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
questions.explanation: 'So' takes the positive degree: 'No other place in this country is so good as Gulmarg.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Rare species “of frogs were very quicker” identified by Stella.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb, so 'very quickly', not 'very quicker'.

questions.text: What does the idiom ‘Bite the bullet’ mean?
options: Give someone a piece of advice
Face a difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4515 × 5 – 431 ÷ 3 + 821 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs the expression becomes 4515 ÷ 5 + 431 × 3 − 821 = 903 + 1293 − 821 = 1375.

questions.text: 31 is related to 152 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 47 is related to 168. To which of the following is 66 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to the number 121 more than it: 31 + 121 = 152 and 47 + 121 = 168, so 66 + 121 = 187.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. In three of the four pairs, the same pattern is applied and hence they form a group. Select the number-pair that DOES NOT belong to this group. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 335 - 119, 317 - 101 and 308 - 92 the second number is 216 less than the first. 358 − 216 = 142, not 152, so 358 - 152 is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'NAME’ is written as 'FNBO' and 'NANO' is written as 'POBO’. How will 'NAIL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse and every letter moves one step forward: NAME → EMAN → FNBO, NANO → ONAN → POBO. So NAIL → LIAN → MJBO.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: Each pair names a shape and its number of sides. A hexagon has 6 sides, not 8, so 'Hexagon - 8 sides' does not belong.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘NIGHTMARES’ is re-arranged in the English alphabetical order from left to right?
questions.explanation: In alphabetical order NIGHTMARES becomes A E G H I M N R S T. Comparing position by position, G (3rd), H (4th), M (6th) and R (8th) stay where they were: four letters.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 – 4 ÷ 9 + 80 × 10 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 + 4 × 9 − 80 ÷ 10 = 5 + 36 − 8 = 33.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (149, 213) (168, 232) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In both pairs the second number is 64 more than the first (149 + 64 = 213, 168 + 64 = 232). Only (153, 217) follows the same rule.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MEK: NVP :: GYT: TBG :: JWH:?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): M→N, E→V, K→P and G→T, Y→B, T→G. So J→Q, W→D, H→S, giving QDS.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No card is a parcel. All cards are envelopes. Some envelopes are bags. Conclusions: I. All envelopes can never be parcels. II. No card is a bag. III. At least some bags are postcards.
questions.explanation: Some envelopes are cards and no card is a parcel, so not every envelope can be a parcel: conclusion I follows. Nothing links cards and bags for certain (II), and postcards are not mentioned at all (III).

questions.text: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? UE 88, VG 84, WI 80, XK76, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run U, V, W, X, so next is Y; the second letters skip one each time (E, G, I, K), so next is M; the number falls by 4 (88, 84, 80, 76), so next is 72: YM72.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. L_P_QS_K_P_S_KP_Q_L_ _PQS
questions.explanation: Filling the blanks with K P L P Q L P S K P makes the block LKPPQS repeat four times: LKPPQS LKPPQS LKPPQS LKPPQS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘what where how’ is written as ‘aa dd ff’; ‘where there that’ is written as ‘dd zz pp’ and ‘which what here’ is written as ‘ff kk ll’. How is ‘how’ written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'where' is common to the first two sentences and 'dd' to their codes, so where = dd; 'what' is common to the first and third, as is 'ff', so what = ff. The remaining word of the first sentence, 'how', is therefore 'aa'.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tears are drops. Some drops are streams. All streams are rivers. Conclusions: I. All tears can never be rivers. II. Some drops are rivers. III. All tears being streams is a possibility.
options: Both II and III conclusion follow
Both I and II conclusion follow
questions.explanation: Some drops are streams and all streams are rivers, so some drops are rivers: II follows. No statement rules out every tear being a stream, so III is a possibility. I is not definite.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? YZUW, ?, QTQU, MQOT, INMS
questions.explanation: Letter by letter the terms move back by fixed steps: first letters −4 (Y, U, Q, M, I), second −3 (Z, W, T, Q, N), third −2 (U, S, Q, O, M) and fourth −1 (W, V, U, T, S). The missing term is UWSV.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’, ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A / B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A = B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. Which of the following means A is the daughter of K? i. A + K / J – P = D ii. J % P = K + A = D iii. K + A / P – D % J iv. D + K = A / P – J
questions.explanation: In K + A / P − D % J, 'K + A' means K is the mother of A, and 'A / P' means A is the wife of P, so A is female. A is therefore the daughter of K.

questions.text: 19 is related to 209 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 27 is related to 297. To which of the following is 61 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 11: 19 × 11 = 209 and 27 × 11 = 297, so 61 × 11 = 671.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 10, 41, ?, 1237
questions.explanation: Each term is the previous one multiplied by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 in turn, plus 1: 1×2+1 = 3, 3×3+1 = 10, 10×4+1 = 41, 41×5+1 = 206 and 206×6+1 = 1237.

questions.text: Details about Sudarshana lake is given in a rock inscription at Girnar (Junagarh), which was composed to record the achievements of the Shaka ruler _________.
questions.explanation: The Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of the Shaka ruler Rudradaman I records the repair of the Sudarshana lake and his achievements.

questions.text: ___________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
questions.explanation: Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is the industry association of microfinance lenders that works as a self-regulatory organisation for the sector.

questions.text: Which article has a similar provision to that of Article 32 and deals with writ jurisdiction?
questions.explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs; Article 226 gives the High Courts a similar, wider writ jurisdiction.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a condition for the President’s office in India?
options: He shall not hold any office of profit.
The allowances shall not be diminished during his term of office.
He shall not be entitled, without payment of rent, to use his official residence.
He shall not be a member of either House of the Parliament.

questions.text: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?
options: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium
questions.explanation: In NCERT's usage 'monoecious' denotes the bisexual condition, with male and female reproductive structures together; of the options, that is a flower with both androecium and gynoecium.

questions.text: Mohan Veena player, Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the ____________ Award in the year 1994.
questions.explanation: Mohan Veena player Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won a Grammy Award in 1994 for the album 'A Meeting by the River', recorded with Ry Cooder.

questions.text: Who is Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology as of July 2023?
questions.explanation: In July 2023 Dr Jitendra Singh was Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology.

questions.text: Which of the following decomposition reactions is NOT a redox reaction?
questions.explanation: When calcium carbonate decomposes (CaCO3 → CaO + CO2), no element changes its oxidation state, so it is not a redox reaction; the other three decompositions involve oxidation and reduction.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?

questions.text: The head office of Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is located in ________.
questions.explanation: The head office of the Board of Control for Cricket in India is in Mumbai.

questions.text: When the analysis of population density is done by calculating it through net cultivated area, then the measure is termed as:

questions.explanation: Mahendravarman I was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty of Kanchipuram.

questions.text: What challenge does foreign investment often face in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's answer is an inconsistent regulatory environment: rules and approvals that keep changing make long-term foreign investment uncertain.

questions.text: Which Indian among the following has his name in Time Magazine’s list of ‘100 most influential people of 2021’?

questions.text: A grocer professes to sell rice at the cost price, but uses a fake weight of 870 g for 1 kg. Find his profit percentage (correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: He gives 870 g but charges for 1000 g, so his profit is 130/870 × 100 ≈ 14.94%.

questions.text: In a circular race of 840 m, A and B start running in the same direction at the same time from the same point at the speeds of 6 m/s and 12 m/s, respectively. After how much time will they meet next?
questions.explanation: Running in the same direction, B gains 12 − 6 = 6 m/s on A. They meet again when B has gained one full lap: 840 ÷ 6 = 140 s.

questions.text: Let O be the centre of the circle and AB and CD are two parallel chords on the same side of the radius. OP is perpendicular to AB and OQ is perpendicular to CD. If AB = 10 cm, CD = 24 cm and PQ = 7 cm, then the diameter (in cm) of the circle is equal to:
questions.explanation: The half-chords are 5 cm and 12 cm. With radius r, OP = √(r² − 25) and OQ = √(r² − 144), and with both chords on the same side OP − OQ = 7. r = 13 fits (12 − 5 = 7), so the diameter is 26 cm.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is sufficient to conclude that two triangles are congruent?
options: One side and one angle of both triangles are equal.
These have two equal sides and the same perimeter.
These have the same area and the same base.
These have the same base and the same height.
questions.explanation: If two sides are equal and the perimeters are equal, the third sides are equal too, so the triangles are congruent by SSS. None of the other conditions fixes all three sides.

questions.text: Fill pipe P is 21 times faster than fill pipe Q. If Q can fill a cistern in 110 minutes, find the time it takes to fill the cistern when both fill pipes are opened together.
questions.explanation: Q fills 1/110 of the cistern a minute and P, 21 times faster, fills 21/110. Together they fill 22/110 = 1/5 a minute, so they take 5 minutes.

questions.text: R pays ₹100 to P with ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins. The total number of coins used for paying are 40. What is the number of coins of denomination ₹5 in the payment?
questions.explanation: With a coins of ₹5, b of ₹2 and c of ₹1: 5a + 2b + c = 100 and a + b + c = 40, so 4a + b = 60 and a cannot exceed 15. Of the options only 13 works (b = 8, c = 19).

questions.text: The radii of the two cones are in the ratio of 2 : 5 and their volumes are in the ratio of 3 : 5. What is the ratio of their heights?
questions.explanation: Volume = (1/3)πr²h, so height is proportional to V/r². Ratio of heights = (3/5) ÷ (4/25) = (3/5) × (25/4) = 15 : 4.

questions.text: Which of the following can be the value of ‘k’ so that the number 217924k is divisible by 6?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 6 the number must be even and its digit sum divisible by 3. 2 + 1 + 7 + 9 + 2 + 4 = 25, so k must be 2, 5 or 8, and even: of the options, 2.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, y% of the voters did not vote. 10% of the votes cast were declared invalid, while all the valid votes were cast in favour of either of the two candidates. The candidate who got 59.375% of the valid votes cast was declared elected by 2484 votes. If the number of people eligible to vote in that election was 16,000, what is the value of y?
questions.explanation: The winner's margin is 59.375% − 40.625% = 18.75% of valid votes = 2484, so there were 13,248 valid votes. These are 90% of the votes cast, so 14,720 people voted out of 16,000, i.e. 92%. So y = 8.

questions.text: An article is marked at ₹550. If it is sold at a discount of 40%, then the selling price becomes 10% more than its cost price. What is the cost price (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 60% of ₹550 = ₹330, which is 110% of the cost price, so CP = 330 ÷ 1.1 = ₹300.

questions.text: If the sum of two sides of an equilateral triangle is 16 cm, then find the third side.
questions.explanation: All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal. Two sides total 16 cm, so each side, including the third, is 8 cm.

questions.text: The distance between the centres of two circles of radii 22 cm and 10 cm is 37 cm. If the points of contact of a direct common tangent to these circles are M and Q, then find the length of the line segment MQ.
questions.explanation: Length of a direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(37² − 12²) = √(1369 − 144) = √1225 = 35 cm.

questions.text: The average marks (out of 100) of boys and girls in an examination are 75 and 80, respectively. If the average marks of all the students in that examination are 78. Find the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls.
questions.explanation: By alligation, boys : girls = (80 − 78) : (78 − 75) = 2 : 3.

questions.text: Mohan borrows a sum of ₹4,22,092 at the rate of 20% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹21,679 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Mohan clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest = 20% of ₹4,22,092 = ₹84,418.40. After repaying ₹21,679 of principal, ₹4,00,413 remains, earning ₹80,082.60 in the second year. At the end of year two he pays 4,00,413 + 84,418.40 + 80,082.60 = ₹5,64,914.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: 'All fans are brown' gives 'some brown are fans' (I), and 'some brown are chairs' gives 'some chairs are brown' (II). III contradicts 'some chairs are plastic'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’. R – T means ‘R is the father of T’. R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’. R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’. Based on the above, how is F related to C if ‘A + B – C ÷ D * E – F ÷ G’?
questions.explanation: B is the father of C, C is the mother of D, D is the wife of E and E is the father of F. So F's mother D is C's daughter, and F is female because F is the mother of G: F is C's daughter's daughter.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. questions.explanation: The Nile is the chief river of Egypt, as the Irrawaddy is of Myanmar. The Mekong, Colorado and Mississippi do not flow through South Korea, Brazil or Russia.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘It’s your life’ is written as ‘Ao Bo Co’ and ‘It’s your food’ is written as ‘Ba Co Bo’. How will ‘food’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'It's' and 'your' are in both sentences, as are 'Bo' and 'Co'. The remaining words pair up: life = Ao and food = Ba.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will change, if each of the letters in the word ‘SYSTEM’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
