questions.explanation: In the pairs, second = first × 3 + 3: 15 → 48, 12 → 39 and 13 → 42. But 11 × 3 + 3 = 36, not 35, so 11 : 35 is the odd one.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster pair that does NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their positions in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In EJ - OT, KP - UZ and CH - MR each cluster's second letter is 5 places after its first, and the second cluster starts 10 places after the first. PF - OI follows neither rule.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 1604 × 4 – 525 ÷ 5 + 73 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 1604 ÷ 4 + 525 × 5 − 73 = 401 + 2625 − 73 = 2953.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series. BVTO, DTVM, ?, HPZI, JNBG
questions.explanation: Letter by letter: first letters +2 (B, D, F, H, J), second −2 (V, T, R, P, N), third +2 (T, V, X, Z, B) and fourth −2 (O, M, K, I, G). The missing term is FRXK.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. VO39, TM35, RK31, PI27, ?
questions.explanation: Both letters move back two places (V, T, R, P, N and O, M, K, I, G) and the number falls by 4 (39, 35, 31, 27, 23): NG23.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 4 ÷ 6 + 91 × 7 − 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 × 6 − 91 ÷ 7 + 5 = 24 − 13 + 5 = 16.

questions.text: In which part of India does the hot wind ‘Loo’ blow?
questions.explanation: The Loo is the hot, dry wind that blows in the afternoons of May and June over the plains of north and north-west India.

questions.text: The first southern campaign of Alauddin Khilji in 1307-08 AD was led to which of the following regions?
questions.explanation: The 1307-08 campaign, led by Malik Kafur, was against the Yadava kingdom of Devagiri. Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai were attacked in the campaigns that followed.

questions.text: Which of the following can be represented as a functional unit of nature?
questions.explanation: An ecosystem, in which living things and their physical surroundings interact, is called the functional unit of nature.

questions.text: At what latitude does the easterly jet stream blow over peninsular India during the summer months?
questions.explanation: In summer an easterly jet stream blows over the southern part of the peninsula; SSC's key places it at about 14°N.

questions.text: The inaugural match of the Women Premier League 2023 cricket was played in which of the following venues?
questions.explanation: The first Women's Premier League match, Mumbai Indians v Gujarat Giants on 4 March 2023, was played at the D. Y. Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai.

questions.text: When electricity is passed through water, what kind of chemical reaction occurs?
questions.explanation: Passing electricity through water (electrolysis) splits it into hydrogen and oxygen, 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂: a decomposition reaction.

questions.text: Which music-composer duo was honoured with the National Lata Mangeshkar Award for the year 2020?
questions.explanation: The Madhya Pradesh government's National Lata Mangeshkar Award for 2020 went to the composer duo Anand-Milind.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Govindji Nartanalaya located?
questions.explanation: Govindaji Nartanalaya is an institution of Manipuri dance in Manipur.

questions.text: In which state of India is Kund or Tanka used for water harvesting?
questions.explanation: Kunds or tankas are covered underground pits that store rainwater, a traditional water-harvesting method of the Thar desert in Rajasthan.

questions.text: When was the High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, 2021 introduced in Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 30 November 2021, during the Winter Session.

questions.text: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
questions.explanation: Icterus is the medical name for jaundice, in which bilirubin builds up and turns the skin and the whites of the eyes yellow.

questions.text: Which of the following inscriptions of Rudradaman happened to be the first royal inscription of early India composed in chaste Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: Rudradaman's Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription of about 150 CE is the first long royal inscription of early India in chaste Sanskrit.

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, in rural India, which state has the maximum female workforce participation rate?
questions.explanation: According to Census 2011, Himachal Pradesh had the highest female work participation rate in rural India of the states listed.

questions.text: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja, celebrated mainly in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh, is devoted to the Sun God and his wife Usha.

questions.text: At which Olympics did Gagan Narang win a bronze medal?
questions.explanation: Gagan Narang won bronze in the men's 10 m air rifle at the London 2012 Olympics.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was a Madrasa opened in Kolkata to promote the study of Arabic, Persian and Islamic law?
questions.explanation: Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781 to promote the study of Arabic, Persian and Islamic law.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name of tertiarybutyl alcohol?
questions.explanation: Tertiary-butyl alcohol is (CH₃)₃C–OH: a three-carbon chain (propane) with both the –OH and a methyl group on carbon 2, i.e. 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the executive power of the union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a state as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose?
questions.explanation: Article 257(1), on the control of the Union over states in certain cases, says exactly this.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under the leadership of which of the following revolutionaries was Chittagong Armoury Raid conducted?
questions.explanation: The Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930 was led by Surya Sen ('Masterda').

questions.text: What is the relationship between interest rate and demand for money?
questions.explanation: The higher the interest rate, the more it costs to hold money instead of interest-bearing assets, so the demand for money falls: the relation is inverse.

questions.text: The government of which of the following states created a draft policy in 2022 for senior citizens on the basis of article 41, which aims to form a directorate for the welfare of senior citizens?
questions.explanation: In 2022 Tamil Nadu released a draft state policy for senior citizens, based on Article 41, that proposed a directorate for their welfare.

questions.text: In the year 1952, who among the following lent his voice for the film ‘Amar Bhupali’, which was being produced in two languages simultaneously and he sang in both Bengali and Marathi ?
questions.explanation: Manna Dey sang in both the Marathi and the Bengali versions of 'Amar Bhupali'.

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly defines the green revolution?
options: It is a new strategy to use green colour for all purposes.
It is a new strategy to increase the share of the forest.
It is a new strategy in agriculture to produce food grains, especially wheat and rice.
It is a new strategy to use only herbal products.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution (from the mid-1960s) used high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation to raise food-grain output, above all of wheat and rice.

questions.text: In 2021, in which of the following states did the Prime Minister lay the foundation stone for the Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University?
questions.explanation: In September 2021 the Prime Minister laid the foundation stone of Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University at Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT correct about Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: They provide guidelines for the governance of the country.
They are morally binding on the government.
They ensure social and economic development.
questions.explanation: Under Article 37 no court can enforce the Directive Principles: they are non-justiciable. So 'They are justiciable in nature' is the incorrect statement.

questions.text: Madhav purchased an item for ₹42,000 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With that amount, he purchased another item and sold it at a gain of 30%. What is the overall gain (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: After a 20% loss he gets 80% of ₹42,000 = ₹33,600. A 30% gain on that gives ₹43,680, so the overall gain is ₹43,680 − ₹42,000 = ₹1,680.

questions.text: Seven years ago, Prachi was four times as old as her daughter was at that time. Four years from now, Prachi will be two-and-a-half times as old as her daughter would then be. Find the sum of the present ages (in years) of Prachi and her daughter.
questions.explanation: Let the daughter be D now and Prachi P. P − 7 = 4(D − 7) and P + 4 = 2.5(D + 4). So 4D − 17 = 2.5D + 10, giving D = 18 and P = 51. Sum = 69.

questions.text: If a sum of ₹5,000 is taken at a simple rate of interest of 15% per annum for 3 years and another sum of ₹8,000 is taken at a simple interest of 12% per annum for 4 years, the positive difference of the interests paid is:

Let C be a circle with centre O and P be an external point to C. Let PA and PB be two tangents to C with A and B being the points of tangency, respectively. If PA and PB are inclined to each other at an angle of 60°, then find ∠POA.
questions.explanation: OA is perpendicular to the tangent PA, and PO bisects ∠APB, so ∠APO = 30°. In right triangle OAP, ∠POA = 90° − 30° = 60°.

questions.text: The average temperature of a city for the first sixteen days of January is 22°C, and the average temperature for the last sixteen days of the same month is 26°C. If the average temperature for the entire month is 24°C, what is the temperature on the sixteenth day?
questions.explanation: January has 31 days, so day 16 is in both groups. Days 1-16 total 16 × 22 = 352 and days 16-31 total 16 × 26 = 416. Their sum counts day 16 twice: 352 + 416 − 31 × 24 = 768 − 744 = 24°C.

questions.text: At present, A is thrice as old as B. C is 5 years elder than B. The sum of the ages of A, B, C is 75 years. The ratio of the age of B five years ago to the age of A three years from now is:
questions.explanation: A = 3B and C = B + 5, so 3B + B + B + 5 = 75, B = 14 and A = 42. Five years ago B was 9; in three years A will be 45. 9 : 45 = 1 : 5.

questions.text: A person earns ₹16,000 per month and spends 80% of his income and saves the remaining amount. If his income increases by 20% and expenditure by 10%, find the percentage of increase in his savings.
questions.explanation: Savings now = 20% of ₹16,000 = ₹3,200. New income = ₹19,200 and new expenditure = 110% of ₹12,800 = ₹14,080, so new savings = ₹5,120. Increase = 1,920/3,200 = 60%.

questions.text: The marked price of an article is 26% more than its cost price. If a discount of 32% is given, what will be the loss percentage?
questions.explanation: Take cost price = 100. Marked price = 126 and selling price = 68% of 126 = 85.68, so the loss is 14.32%.

questions.text: Varun and Sandeep started for a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 1635 m with the speeds of 90 km/h and 108 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in s) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.explanation: In the same direction the relative speed is 108 − 90 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. The faster car gains one full lap of 1635 m in 1635/5 = 327 s.

questions.text: From a circle with the radius of 15.75 cm, a sector with the arc length of 11 cm is cut off. Find the area (in cm²) of this sector.
questions.explanation: Area of a sector = ½ × arc length × radius = ½ × 11 × 15.75 = 86.625 cm².

questions.text: If x varies inversely as y and x = 2 when y = 6, then the value of y when x = 3 is:
questions.explanation: In inverse variation xy is constant: 2 × 6 = 12. With x = 3, y = 12/3 = 4.

questions.text: Without doing the actual division, find the remainder when 28735429 is divided by 9.
questions.explanation: A number leaves the same remainder on division by 9 as its digit sum: 2+8+7+3+5+4+2+9 = 40, and 40 = 4 × 9 + 4, so the remainder is 4.

questions.text: Simplify the following: 21− 4.9 ÷ 7 + 3.9 × 0.4 + 0.9
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication first: 4.9 ÷ 7 = 0.7 and 3.9 × 0.4 = 1.56. Then 21 − 0.7 + 1.56 + 0.9 = 22.76.

questions.text: Pipes M, N and S can fill a tank in 25, 50 and 100 minutes, respectively. Initially, pipes N and S are kept open for 10 minutes, and then pipe N is shut while pipe M is opened. Pipe S is closed 15 minutes before the tank overflows. How much time (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank if the three pipes work in this pattern?
questions.explanation: Per minute M fills 4%, N 2% and S 1% of the tank. N and S fill 30% in the first 10 minutes, and M alone fills 60% in the last 15. The remaining 10% takes M and S together (5% a minute) 2 minutes. Total = 10 + 2 + 15 = 27 minutes.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The homework must be done by you.
options: You should have done the homework.
questions.explanation: 'Must be done by you' is the passive of 'must do': 'You must do the homework.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Pollution levels have increased so “largely” that they are almost killing us.
questions.explanation: 'Largely' means mostly, and does not say how much the levels rose. SSC's key picks 'highly' (to a high degree); 'primarily' and 'chiefly' mean the same as 'largely', and 'slowly' contradicts 'almost killing us'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (a) the use of animal research (b) throughout the past century (c) and it continues to be used to understand many diseases (d) has been of considerable importance (e) in the field of scientific and medical advancements
questions.explanation: Subject (a) 'the use of animal research', verb (d) 'has been of considerable importance', where (e) 'in the field of…', when (b) 'throughout the past century', then the added clause (c): adebc.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break a leg
options: Give advice on maintaining physical health.
Wish someone good luck before a performance.
Suggest taking a short break during work.
Encourage someone to engage in risky activities.
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is said to a performer before going on stage, to wish them good luck.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Spreading awareness about the rights of the consumers and the relief open to them in case they “did not get their money’s worth” of goods and service has rightly been identified as the first priority.
options: were unable to get their money’s worth
did not getting their money’s worth
will not get their money’s worth
questions.explanation: SSC's key picks 'were unable to get their money's worth', which says plainly that the consumers could not obtain fair value. 'Did not getting' is ungrammatical, and 'will not get' clashes with the past tense of the clause.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'abysmal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. If you want to be a good detective, it helps to have an “inquisitive” nature.
questions.explanation: 'Inquisitive' means eager to find things out. Of the options only 'disinterested', used here for showing no interest, points the opposite way; 'intrusive' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who does not show response to good or bad
questions.explanation: A 'stoic' bears pain and pleasure alike without showing feeling.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. These can turn around to track stars with the rotation of Earth. B. Observatories are places to study place. C. They are mostly built on the mountain tops. D. Telescopes are placed in the dome-shaped roof of the building.
questions.explanation: B introduces observatories, C ('They') says where they are built, D describes the telescopes in the dome, and A ('These') says what the telescopes do: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: I will definitely attend the conference.
I will definetely attend the conference.
I will definately attend the conference.
I will definitly attend the conference.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'definitely'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (O) as it was the last one of the evening (P) the city bus was overcrowded (Q) and this gave an opportunity (R) to the pickpockets (S) to try their skill
questions.explanation: 'The city bus was overcrowded (P) as it was the last one of the evening (O) and this gave an opportunity (Q) to the pickpockets (R) to try their skill (S).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Raju’s job as a clerk seemed to be “bad at first because of the low salary, but resulted in something good happening later” because it saved him from being unemployed.
questions.explanation: Something that seems bad at first but turns out well is 'a blessing in disguise'.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Scary
questions.explanation: 'Scary' means frightening; its opposite is 'comforting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Abundant
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means plentiful: 'ample'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. I would love to “organise” the farewell party at my house.
questions.explanation: To 'organise' an event is to plan and 'arrange' it.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Every students in the hostel decided to travel to Delhi to witness the Republic Day parade.
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular noun: 'Every student in the hostel'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The meal was not prepared by us.
options: We did not preparing the meal.
We did not prepare the meal.
We had not prepare the meal.
questions.explanation: 'Was not prepared by us' is simple past passive; the active is 'We did not prepare the meal.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Berserk
questions.explanation: 'Berserk' means wild and out of control: 'demented' (crazed).

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. By this time next year / I will had graduated from college / and starting my first job / in the field of marketing.
options: I will had graduated from college
questions.explanation: The future perfect is 'will have graduated', not 'will had graduated'.

questions.text:

questions.explanation: After a comma, the relative pronoun for a thing (smallpox) is 'which'; 'that' is not used after a comma.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. From the beginning (1)_________ the eighteenth century, the ladies of European cities covered (2)_______ faces in layers of paint and powder. This particular fashion was largely brought (3) __________ by the urgent need to disguise the ravages of smallpox, (4)_________ left their faces pitted and scarred. During this same period, the ‘beauty spot’ was introduced to cover (5) __________ a facial defect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'cover up' a defect is to hide it.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CWE:ZFX ::PYT:MDI :: KIL:?
questions.explanation: In each pair the positions of matching letters add up to 29: C(3)→Z(26), W(23)→F(6), E(5)→X(24), and P→M, Y→D, T→I likewise. So K(11)→R(18), I(9)→T(20) and L(12)→Q(17): RTQ.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MFT, NIS, PLQ, SON, WRJ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 (M, N, P, S, W, so next B); second letters +3 (F, I, L, O, R, so U); third letters −1, −2, −3, −4, −5 (T, S, Q, N, J, so E): BUE.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 36 – 84, 66 – 154 and 72 – 168 the two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7. 33 × 7/3 = 77, not 72, so 33 – 72 is the odd one.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 24 ÷ 3 – 4 × 2 + 6 × 5 +12 = 50
The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letter in the word ‘JANITOR’ is arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: JANITOR in alphabetical order is A I J N O R T. Position by position (J/A, A/I, N/J, I/N, T/O, O/R, R/T) no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In PSUV, FIKL and TWYZ the letters move +3, +2, +1. BEHI moves +3, +3, +1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. P _ A A _ _ Z A _V _ _ A _ _
questions.explanation: With Z, V, P, A, P, Z, A, V in the blanks the series reads PZAAV PZAAV PZAAV: the block PZAAV repeats.

questions.text: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? XF 11 , YI 15, ZL 19 , AO 23, ?
questions.explanation: First letters run X, Y, Z, A, so next is B; second letters move +3 (F, I, L, O), so next is R; the number rises by 4 (11, 15, 19, 23), so next is 27: BR 27.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SILK’ is written as ‘TIML’ and ‘INSECT’ is written as ‘IOTEDU’. How will ‘CHANGE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one letter forward and each vowel stays: SILK → TIML and INSECT → IOTEDU. So CHANGE → DIAOHE.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 321 – 371 ÷ 22 + 216 × 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 321 + 371 × 22 − 216 ÷ 6 = 321 + 8162 − 36 = 8447.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (12, 145) (9, 82)
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 1: 12² + 1 = 145 and 9² + 1 = 82. Likewise 14² + 1 = 197.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the sister of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P ÷ Q × R − M + T’?
questions.explanation: P is the mother of Q; Q, R and M are siblings; and M is the son of T. So T is the other parent of P's children: P's husband.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 35, 38, 43, 50, 59, ___
questions.explanation: The differences are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next is +11: 59 + 11 = 70.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (19, 456, 6) (16, 320, 5)
questions.explanation: In each set, first × third × 4 = second: 19 × 6 × 4 = 456 and 16 × 5 × 4 = 320. Likewise 18 × 9 × 4 = 648.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (34, 47, 62) (119, 142, 167) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SET’ is coded as ‘37’ and ‘MIX’ is coded as ‘35’. How will ‘WAR’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its position counted from Z (A = 26, B = 25, …, Z = 1) and the code is their sum: SET = 8 + 22 + 7 = 37 and MIX = 14 + 18 + 3 = 35. So WAR = 4 + 26 + 9 = 39.

questions.text: What is the length of Indian Railways network, according to Railway Yearbook 2019- 20?
questions.explanation: According to the Indian Railways Year Book 2019-20, the network's route length was 67,956 km.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest crustal plate on Earth with an area of over 103,000,000 km²?
questions.explanation: The Pacific plate, at over 103 million km², is the largest of the Earth's lithospheric plates.

questions.text: ‘Nuakhai’ is the state festival of:
questions.explanation: Nuakhai, the harvest festival at which the new rice is first offered, is the state festival of Odisha, celebrated mainly in western Odisha.

questions.text: Which of the following is a straight-chain alkyl carboxylic acid with the chemical formula CH₃CH₂CH₂CO₂H?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH has four carbon atoms: butanoic (butyric) acid. Methanoic, ethanoic and propionic acids have one, two and three.

questions.text: Who among the following was the youngest instrumentalist to be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award of India in 2002?
questions.explanation: Tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain received the Padma Bhushan in 2002. Of the others, Bhimsen Joshi was a vocalist, and Ravi Shankar and Bismillah Khan received theirs in the 1960s.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits providing of any religious instruction in the educational institutions maintained by the State?
questions.explanation: Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.text: Article 77 of the Indian Constitution deals with the __________.
options: oath of office by the Vice-President
conduct of business of the Government of India
term of office of the Vice-President
questions.explanation: Article 77 covers the conduct of business of the Government of India: all its executive action is taken in the President's name.

questions.text: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 deals with subsistence allowance in which of the following Sections?
questions.explanation: Section 5 of the 2019 Act entitles a Muslim woman against whom triple talaq is pronounced to subsistence allowance for herself and her dependent children.

questions.text: In which year was the 'Naye Bharat Ke Sapne' campaign launched by Meta and the Ministry of Women?
questions.explanation: Meta launched the 'Naye Bharat Ke Sapne' campaign with the Ministry of Women and Child Development in 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Fats and oils get reduced over time and smell bad.
Antioxidants are added to foods containing fats and oil to prevent oxidation.
Chips manufacturers usually flush bags of chips with Nitrogen to prevent the chips from getting ranicid.
Fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid.
questions.explanation: Fats and oils go rancid because they are oxidised, not reduced, which is why antioxidants are added and chip bags are flushed with nitrogen. So the first statement is incorrect.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which of the following Acts was the power to rule India, transferred from the English East India Company to the British Crown?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, transferred the power to govern India from the East India Company to the British Crown.

questions.text: Which of the following countries won the first men’s Asian Hockey Championship trophy?
questions.explanation: India won the first men's Asian Champions Trophy, held in Ordos, China, in 2011.

questions.text: Silappathikaram (the Jewelled Anklet), the earliest epic poem in Tamil was written in the 5th - 6th Century CE by _________.
questions.explanation: Silappathikaram was written by Ilango Adigal; Sittalai Sattanar wrote its sequel, Manimekalai.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?.
options: The five-year plan focuses mostly on private intervention in the economy.
The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
The five-year plan always focused on the growth of the tertiary sector.
A five-year plan always stresses market-oriented activities.
questions.explanation: A five-year plan sets out long-term government intervention in the economy; it is not about private intervention or market-oriented activity alone.

questions.text: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ___________ in plain areas.
questions.explanation: Under PMAY-G the Centre and the States share the cost of unit assistance 60 : 40 in plain areas, and 90 : 10 in the north-eastern and Himalayan states.

questions.text: Who was the revenue minister during the reign of Akbar?
questions.explanation: Raja Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and devised the zabti system of land revenue.

questions.text: Hot local wind that flows over north India in summer is known as:
questions.explanation: The Loo is the hot, dry wind of the north Indian plains in May and June. The Chinook blows in North America, and mango showers are pre-monsoon rains in the south.

questions.text: As per the definition of Census of India, a ‘marginal worker’ is a person who works for:
options: more than 183 days (or six months) in a year
less than 183 days (or six months) in a year
questions.explanation: The Census of India counts as a marginal worker anyone who worked for less than 183 days (six months) of the year; 183 days or more makes a main worker.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Nrityagram, an Odissi dance institution, located?
questions.explanation: Nrityagram, the Odissi dance village founded by Protima Gauri in 1990, is near Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.text: At which Olympics was Kho-Kho featured in an exhibition in the main stadium?
questions.explanation: Kho-kho was shown as a demonstration sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

questions.text: Which of the following goods needs further transformation in the economic process?
questions.explanation: Intermediate goods, such as raw materials and parts, are used up in making other goods, so they still need further transformation; final goods do not.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following devised the system of ‘Subsidiary Alliance’?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley, Governor-General from 1798 to 1805, devised the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.text: Which of the following is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine developed in 1952?
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated (killed) polio vaccine in 1952; Sabin's oral vaccine uses live, weakened virus.

questions.text: Which of the following personalities is a Padma Shri awardee folk singer from the state of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Ajita Srivastava, a folk singer from Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2022. Teejan Bai is a Pandavani singer from Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: A number is first increased by 12% and then increased by 23%. The number, so obtained, is now decreased by 34%. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (nearest to an integer)?
questions.explanation: 1.12 × 1.23 × 0.66 = 0.909, so the number ends about 9.1% below where it started: a 9% decrease to the nearest integer.

questions.text: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 6%. Stock B represents 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. Stock C represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock D represents the remaining 30% of the portfolio and has a negative-return of 5%. What is the average return of the portfolio?

A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of 600 metres. The thief started running and the policeman chased him. The thief and policeman are running at speeds of 12 km/h and 15 km/h, respectively. Find the time (in minutes) required for the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 15 − 12 = 3 km/h = 50 m a minute on the thief, so he closes 600 m in 12 minutes.

questions.text: What is the perimeter (in cm, rounded off to one decimal place) of the sector of a circle with a radius of 10 cm and of angle 30°? (Use π = 3.14)
If 7845K854 is divisible by 11, then what is the value of K?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 11 the sums of alternate digits must differ by 0 or a multiple of 11. Odd places: 7 + 4 + K + 5 = 16 + K; even places: 8 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 25. 25 − (16 + K) = 0 gives K = 9.

questions.text: In a ΔPQR, the bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet at point O, inside the triangle. If ∠QOR = 107°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.explanation: Where the bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet, ∠QOR = 90° + ∠P/2. So 107° = 90° + ∠P/2 and ∠P = 34°.

questions.text: If the equations 4x + (k − 2)y + 3 = 0 and (k − 2)x + 9y − 5 = 0 (k > 0) are parallel, then find the value of k² + 6.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have proportional x and y coefficients: 4/(k − 2) = (k − 2)/9, so (k − 2)² = 36 and k = 8 (as k > 0). Then k² + 6 = 70.

questions.text: Ramesh has ₹18,000. He deposited ₹7,000 in a bank at the rate of 5% per annum and ₹6,000 in other bank at the rate of 6% per annum simple interest. If he received ₹1,160 as simple interest at the end of one year, then the rate of interest per annum on rest of the capital is equal to:
questions.explanation: The first two deposits earn 5% of ₹7,000 + 6% of ₹6,000 = ₹350 + ₹360 = ₹710. The remaining ₹5,000 earned ₹1,160 − ₹710 = ₹450, which is 9%.

questions.text: In a clearance sale, a sari whose marked price was ₹10,490 is now sold for ₹9,441. What is the discount percentage on the sari?
questions.explanation: Discount = ₹10,490 − ₹9,441 = ₹1,049, which is 10% of the marked price.

questions.text: Two triangles EFG and HIJ are congruent. If the area of ΔEFG is 124 cm², then the area of ΔHIJ will be:
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles are identical in shape and size, so their areas are equal: 124 cm².

questions.text: A pipe can fill an overhead tank in 12 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom, it is filled in 18 hours. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it?
questions.explanation: The pipe fills 1/12 of the tank an hour, but with the leak only 1/18, so the leak empties 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36 an hour: 36 hours for a full tank.

questions.text: If the length, breadth, and height of a cuboid is 8 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm, respectively, then the volume (in cm³) of the cuboid is:
questions.explanation: Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h = 8 × 4 × 6 = 192 cm³.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. I receieved a parcel in the mail today.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'received' ('i' before 'e' except after 'c').

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An order of law requiring people to remain indoors
questions.explanation: A curfew is an order requiring people to stay indoors, usually between set hours.

questions.text: Which of the following idioms means ‘to steal from a shop’?
questions.explanation: A 'five-finger discount' is slang for shoplifting.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The tea at this café is best than at the Costa Café in our office.
questions.explanation: Two things are compared, so the comparative is needed: 'is better than', not 'is best than'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Edible
questions.explanation: 'Edible' means fit to be eaten. Of the options only 'nutritive' (nourishing) is close; 'noxious' and 'noisome' mean harmful or offensive.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Morbid compulsion to consume alcohol continuously
questions.explanation: Dipsomania is a morbid craving for alcohol; kleptomania is a compulsion to steal.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P. having the opportunity of observing people’s Q. we respect and appreciate their point of views R. the advantage of travelling different places and S. culture, custom and lifestyle, is that
questions.explanation: 'The advantage of travelling different places and (R) having the opportunity of observing people's (P) culture, custom and lifestyle, is that (S) we respect and appreciate their point of views (Q).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The elaborate syllabi had to be ________(summarised) to make a presentation in the UGC assessment meeting.
questions.explanation: To 'recapitulate' is to summarise; 'expanded', 'prolonged' and 'lengthened' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The question papers are placed in the lockers of the school in a way that they “can’t be reached”.
questions.explanation: Something that cannot be reached is 'inaccessible'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'mischievous', with no 'i' before '-ous'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The painting was admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
options: Art enthusiasts from around the world have admired the painting.
Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.
The painting was being admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
The painting has been admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
questions.explanation: 'Was admired by' is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: 'Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Miserable
questions.explanation: 'Miserable' means very unhappy; its opposite is 'cheerful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Fatima was “at her wits’ end” trying to decide on a serene place for spending the holidays in.
options: So worried, confused or annoyed that she became unconscious
So calm and composed that she knows what to do next
So worried, confused or annoyed that she does not know what to do next
So worried, confused or annoyed that she insulted others for no reason
questions.explanation: To be 'at one's wits' end' is to be so worried or confused that one does not know what to do next.

questions.text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. (Each participant have) performed well.
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'Each participant has performed well.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. He will be made President by the people.
options: He will be made President by the people.
By the people, he shall be made the President.
The people will make him President.
People will be making him the President.
questions.explanation: 'Will be made' is the future passive of 'will make': 'The people will make him President.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Taut
questions.explanation: 'Taut' means stretched tight: 'tight'. 'Slack' and 'flaccid' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Confiscate
questions.explanation: To 'confiscate' is to take away by authority: to 'seize'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. He has the ________ to express his thoughts.
questions.explanation: He has the 'right' (the entitlement) to express his thoughts; 'write' and 'rite' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. There are many factories in the “operative” area of the city.
questions.explanation: An area full of factories is an 'industrial' area; 'industrious' means hard-working.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I are dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.
questions.explanation: 'I' takes 'am': 'I am dancing'.
